items.title: Early 2027 Launch Planned as Mississauga Opens Its Whistleblower Hotline to the Public
items.summary: According to a staff report set to go before Mississauga's general committee on Wednesday, the city plans to launch an expanded whistleblower hotline for residents sometime in the first three months of 2027. The city established its original Whistleblower Program in 2014, giving employees a confidential channel to anonymously flag workplace wrongdoing, but the new fraud and waste hotline will extend that same option to the general public. Amy Truong, the city's internal audit director, wrote in the report that the program has spent the past decade supporting accountability, ethical conduct and a workplace culture where concerns can be raised without fear of reprisal. The report describes the expanded hotline as an independent and confidential reporting mechanism meant to strengthen accountability and reinforce public trust in the integrity of city operations. Once it is running, both city workers and members of the public will be able to use it to report concerns tied to fraud, waste or wrongdoing that could affect the city's operations. Truong's report also frames the changes as an effort to strengthen transparency and public confidence in how the city governs and oversees itself. The move follows discussions among councillors and staff back in March about whether Mississauga should also hire an auditor general to bolster public accountability.

items.title: A Report of an Armed Man in Cooksville Led Police to Four Arrests and $65,000 in Drugs
items.summary: According to CTV News, Peel Regional Police say four people have been arrested after a September 7 call reporting a man armed with a gun inside a vehicle near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street West, in the city's Cooksville area. Officers who responded found the man in possession of an illegal firearm along with a separate loaded magazine, according to police. A search of the scene turned up a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl that police estimated to be worth about $65,000. Investigators later executed a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, where three more people were arrested. Police say Olamilekan Jimoh, 26, of Mississauga, faces the most charges, including careless storage of a firearm, failing to comply with an undertaking, and four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Modupe Abijo, 52, and Omobodunrin Jimoh, 28, both of Mississauga, were each charged with four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking, while Cleo Romi Reynods, 45, of Toronto, was charged with failing to comply with a release order.

items.title: Vehicle Owners, Not Homeowners, Would Take the Hit Under Mississauga's Proposed Lawn-Parking Fines
items.summary: According to a staff report going to Mississauga's general committee on September 23, the city is considering a standalone bylaw that would fine vehicle owners, not property owners, for parking on residential lawns and other landscaped areas. The report recommends banning parking, standing and stopping on grass, gardens and other soft landscaped surfaces on residential properties, with fines set at $150 for standard vehicles and $375 for heavy or recreational vehicles. Violations would be handled through the city's Administrative Penalty System, letting municipal enforcement officers issue a penalty notice directly to a vehicle's registered owner regardless of who was actually driving. Under that system, according to the report, registered owners could dispute a penalty through the city's dispute resolution process. Staff say the change is meant to replace the current approach, which handles lawn parking complaints through the zoning bylaw, a process the report describes as time-consuming and resource-intensive because it requires investigating property conditions rather than simply the act of parking, along with mandatory warning periods, reinspections and potential court proceedings.

items.title: Packed Council Chambers Push Back on a Three-Tower Proposal Near the Etobicoke Border
items.summary: According to a report submitted to the City of Mississauga, residents packed council chambers to oppose an intensification proposal for a property at 4100 Ponytrail Drive and 1850 Rathburn Road East, in the northeast part of the city near the Etobicoke border. The property owner, Chelsea on the Green I Limited Partnership, submitted the proposal to the city in June, seeking to add three 20-storey apartment buildings totalling 695 units to the site. Two existing 18-storey apartment buildings on the property would remain, and the report notes a 25-storey building had previously been approved for the site by the Committee of Adjustment. The proposal requires an Official Plan amendment before it can proceed. Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca raised the development with residents in August as opposition to the plan began building ahead of the council discussion.

items.title: Peel Police Say a Mississauga House Was the Hub of a Multimillion-Dollar Dark Web Drug Ring
items.summary: Police say four people from across the Greater Toronto Area are facing numerous charges after investigators say they dismantled a multimillion-dollar dark web drug trafficking operation allegedly run out of a Mississauga home. According to police, the dark web is a concealed portion of the internet not indexed by conventional search engines and typically accessed only through specialized browsers, which investigators say made tracking the operation more difficult. As the investigation progressed, police say they identified members of the alleged distribution network and zeroed in on several addresses connected to it. Officers executed multiple search warrants on February 20, 2026, including at a residence in Mississauga that police allege was being used in the day-to-day operation of the online drug distribution network. Police say the investigation also recovered a quantity of drugs tied to the network's operations.

items.title: Gun Seized in Cross-Border Trafficking Bust Ties Back to a 2024 Mississauga Killing
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an undercover operation called Project Red Zone, run by the force's Specialized Enforcement Bureau alongside the US Department of Homeland Security and Criminal Intelligence Service Ontario, infiltrated and disrupted a firearms trafficking network operating across the Greater Toronto Area. According to police, the operation seized 23 firearms, 75 grams of cocaine, and more than 950 rounds of ammunition, along with several weapons that are prohibited in Canada. Investigators say one of the recovered firearms has been linked to a March 2024 homicide in Mississauga in which one man was killed and another seriously injured. Police say forensic analysis also tied the seized firearms to 14 separate shootings across the GTA. The investigation determined that 15 of the 23 firearms had originated in the United States before making their way into the trafficking network.

items.title: Washroom Upgrades This Fall Are Just a Preview of a Bigger Celebration Square Overhaul
items.summary: According to INsauga, construction is set to begin this fall at Celebration Square in downtown Mississauga following the venue's seasonal shutdown, though it is only a smaller step ahead of the much larger renovation planned for the outdoor space. The washrooms at the square will be temporarily closed during the work and are expected to reopen in mid-November. The bigger renovation, covering the nearly five-acre public gathering space, could see construction begin toward the end of 2027, the city has said. Plans for that larger project have grown since 2025, when the city first floated more modest improvements for early 2026, into a significantly bigger renewal that will reshape the venue over the next couple of years. Earlier proposals called for bigger, higher-resolution viewing screens and new artificial turf, with that turf-replacement work expected to close the lawn and surrounding pavement to the public for four to six weeks once it begins.
